title: The height-three chromatic overlap: an explicit filtration and its attachments
main_claim: For every prime p>=5 there is an eight-stage filtration of X=L_2 L_{K(3)} S_p^ with cofibers L_2S, Σ^{-1}L_2S, Σ^{-3}L_1S, Σ^{-4}L_1S, Σ^{-5,-6,-8,-9}HQ_p. Its first stage maps to X by the canonical unit, and all connecting maps are given by two signed fracture roofs. Assuming a companion theorem, the first height-one attachment d_3 is nonzero.

issues.description: The nonvanishing of d_3 rests entirely on an external companion result, that L_0L_{K(3)}S -> L_0L_{K(2)}L_{K(3)}S is nonzero on π_{-3}. As stated, that result would rule out any wedge decomposition of X with a Σ^{-3}L_1S summand. Such a summand maps trivially to L_{K(2)}X, and π_{-3}L_0X is one-dimensional, so the companion result refutes the strong chromatic splitting pattern at height 3 for p>=5. The paper does not remark on this consequence. The reduction from the companion statement to d_3≠0 is valid: the completion, localization and scalar-linearity steps all check. The point is a dependency that could not be audited here, not an error in this paper.
issues.evidence: "The top map is nonzero on π_{-3} by [CompanionHeightThreeObstruction, Theorem 1.1]. Hence so is the bottom map." ... "Neither filtration statement asserts the strong wedge or splits its first unit."

coverage:
I read in full: the introduction, Sec 2 (finite fracture construction, the boundary lemma, Prop fracture, Thm attachment-identification, including both rotation signs), Sec 12 (application) and Sec 12-attachment (the canonical-map criterion and the corollary). Checked items:
- Cofiber identifications and the boundary formulas ∂_3=d_3, ∂_4 and ∂_i for i>=5.
- The L_1 / L_J localization roofs.
- Rational degree bookkeeping: L_0L_iS=Q, the exterior basis in degrees 0,-1,-3,-4,-5,-6,-8,-9, injectivity of r, and the quotient basis b.
- The lifting argument in Prop attachment-criterion.
- The descent-section sign computation for ζ (b(t)=-t gives +c_det).

In Sec 7 I read the height-two test theorem. In Sec 9 I read the completion lemma, Prop integral-delta, Thm height-one-maps and the stem -3 bidegree uniqueness (t∈2(p-1)Z, s<=5, so (3,0) for p>=5). In Sec 11 I read all of it: the trace-group cohomology, the building argument for J_3, the unipotent radical, the two presentations of the modification stack, the projective splitting, the arithmetic-weight argument for e_J, trace transport, Witt nonvanishing, the constants-origin square and rational compatibility. In Sec 6 I read the coheight-one comparison statement, the full-norm-weight lemma (exponents ±1,±3 are nonzero mod p-1>=4) and the base-lattice corollary.

Not verified line by line: Secs 4, 5 and 8, the bulk of 6 and 7, and Appendix 10 (Fargues–Fontaine/perfectoid finiteness and decompletion arguments). Those were only spot-read at the statement level.
